ov: A small, nocturnal gliding possum named for its taste for sugary sap and nectar. It glides between trees on membranes stretching from its front to back feet, and looks much like a flying squirrel although the two are not closely related.

why.p: A popular exotic "pocket pet" in several countries, though it needs company to stay healthy.

wt: Males about 140 g, females about 115 g
rg: Coastal forests of southeastern Australia; close relatives live across eastern and northern Australia and New Guinea.
df: Sap, nectar and other sugary foods, plus insects.

cf.tip: The flying squirrel glides the same way but is a rodent; the sugar glider is a marsupial.

fx: For every 1.82 m it glides forward, it drops just 1 m.
It lives up to 9 years in the wild; the oldest known reached 17.8 years.
notes: The animals.js fact is confirmed (glides 50 m or more on a membrane between its fore- and hind limbs). The species was split in 2020, so the strict sugar glider is only in southeastern Australia.
